advisoryNotes: The 2025 paper is used for direct Grade VI prose-question style and three-mark subparts, not as a factual source for these later chapters.
Exact ideal-answer wording is not required; each independent rubric idea earns its mark. No spelling or grammar penalties apply.
The original copyrighted scans remain local. Short quotations in active questions are included in the prompt, so no runtime source image is required.
atomicCoverageInventory: Page 66: father and son wait with guns in a motionless boat on a lake near a red volcanic hill.
Page 66: the father expects fast-moving clouds of birds and tells the boy to shoot quickly.
Page 66: the father asks whether the boy’s gun is loaded and tells him to aim ahead with one shot.
Page 66: the boy is spellbound by huge flocks of teal; watching birds is his passion.
Page 66–67: the flock changes shape, fills the sky and blots out light.
Page 67: father fires repeatedly, misses and says the teal are too high.
Page 67: the boy aims at a leader and shoots it; another bird takes its place.
Page 67: the bird falls behind bulrushes; the boy paddles to recover it.
Page 67: the duck floats with a broken wing compared to a ragged toy-boat sail.
Page 67: the boy is frightened by the injury but relieved when the duck lifts its head.
Page 67–68: the boy wants to take the duck home and look after it.
Page 68: he bandages and feeds the duck, which can never fly again.
Page 68: the boy throws away his gun and says shooting the duck made him sick.
Page 68: the father is initially shocked, then relieved and peaceful that the gun is gone.
Pages 66–69: inline and printed exercises test details, vocabulary, motives and reference to context.
